title: The Debt I Paid Without Leaving My Name
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Last month, I was standing in line at the small pharmacy near my office when I overheard a woman apologizing to the cashier.
Narrator: She was short on money for her son's medicine, and she kept asking if she could pay the rest tomorrow, although the cashier looked unsure.
Narrator: [gently] I didn't know her, and she never noticed me standing behind her, because she was too embarrassed to look up at anyone.
Narrator: I could have simply paid the difference right there and told her it was from me, and she would have thanked me immediately.
Narrator: [carefully] Instead, I asked the cashier quietly to add the missing amount to my own bill, and to please not mention who paid it.
Narrator: The cashier looked confused, so I explained that if the woman knew, she might feel like she owed me something, and I didn't want that.
Narrator: [reflective] I walked out before she finished her purchase, so I never even saw her face clearly, and I still don't know her name.
Narrator: For a few days afterward, I kept wanting to tell my wife what happened, mostly because I felt proud of myself.
Narrator: [honestly] Then I realized that wanting to tell the story was exactly the danger my father warned me about years ago.
Narrator: He said that sharing a deed can endanger sincerity when the real goal becomes praise from an audience.
Narrator: [warmly] So I stayed quiet, although it was harder than I expected, because silence sometimes feels heavier than speaking.
Narrator: Now, whenever I pass that pharmacy, I think of her for a moment, hope her son is healthy, and then I simply keep walking.
Narrator: [sincere] I learned to protect both sincerity and her dignity. A deed may sometimes be discussed for advice or honest reporting, but her private need should never become my proud story.

quiz.question: Where was the narrator standing when he overheard the woman?
options: At a bus stop
At his office desk
In a restaurant
In line at a small pharmacy
quiz.explanation: He was standing in line at the small pharmacy near his office when he overheard her.

quiz.question: What was the woman apologizing about?
options: Being short on money for her son's medicine
Being late
Losing her receipt
Forgetting her wallet at home
quiz.explanation: She was short on money for her son's medicine and asked to pay the rest later.

quiz.question: What did the narrator ask the cashier to do?
options: Refuse to sell the medicine
Add the missing amount to his own bill without saying who paid
Call the woman's family
Give her a discount publicly
quiz.explanation: He asked the cashier to quietly add the missing amount to his bill and not mention who paid.

quiz.question: What did the narrator's father once warn him about?
options: Spending too much money
Talking to strangers
Trusting cashiers
A good deed shared too quickly often loses its sincerity
quiz.explanation: His father warned him that a good deed shared too quickly often loses its sincerity.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator stay quiet about what he did?
options: He didn't want the deed to become a story he tells
He forgot about it
His wife told him not to speak
He was ashamed of helping
quiz.explanation: He learned that some good deeds are meant to stay between him, the moment, and Allah.

quiz.question: Why does the narrator pay without giving his name?
options: He wants the cashier to praise him later
He expects free medicine next month
He wants to protect the woman from embarrassment and obligation
He does not know how much is missing
quiz.explanation: Privacy protects the receiver as well as the giver.

quiz.question: What does “performing for an audience” mean here?
options: Speaking clearly to a cashier
Paying while other customers are present
Doing or telling a deed mainly to gain people’s approval
Working in a public building
quiz.explanation: The phrase describes a change in intention.

quiz.question: Which detail shows that the narrator still has mixed feelings?
options: He forgets the pharmacy address
He asks for his money back
He knows the woman’s full name
He wants to tell someone because he feels proud
quiz.explanation: The desire for praise remains after the action.

quiz.question: When could speaking about charity still be useful?
options: Whenever the giver wants attention
When necessary for advice or transparent reporting without exposing the receiver
Only when the amount is very large
Never under any condition
quiz.explanation: The revised ending gives a careful exception.

quiz.question: What lesson joins intention with respectful charity?
options: Every donation must be secret from one’s family
Cashiers should decide who deserves medicine
Feeling proud always cancels a good deed
Protect sincerity and the dignity of the person receiving help
quiz.explanation: The focus is intention joined with respectful help.
